title: Playing with Pansy Lane in loud pre-microphone bands
summary: He played Saturdays at the Eagles home with Pansy Lane, who carried a gun; all bands were loud before microphones.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: You mentioned Pansy Lane out there.

Yeah I played quite a bit with Pansy Lane in those days. We used to play on Esplanade Avenue, there was a place called the Eagles home. We used to play there every Saturday. And the band was up on the platform right under a tin roof. And you talk about loud, and Pansy never did play soft, you see. And none of the band played soft. Boy it used to ring so loud you couldn't hear yourself think, you know. And the only one I remember in that band was Chink Martin's brother who played bass. Bill Abraham, William Abraham, his last name is Abraham. Chief Martin's right name is Martin Abraham. And Pansy Lane carried a gun all the time. He had some special officer's badge. And every once in a while he'd pull out the gun and say, if you hit the bad note again I'm going to shoot you. Bill used to have fits, he was scared to death of that kind of thing. Boy what a ball that was. And all the old jazz tunes and Pansy used to like to play double eagle and those kind of marches in jazz time. I played with him, well off and on every spot job, you know, from time to time. But I haven't seen him in the last few years now.
Oh he did? That's right. That's right. Boykin's transfer company I believe, then Shane for years. He just played on the side, you know.
Well they had the wig down on Elysian Fields at Shane's.
Yeah I think I remember now, now that you mention it, it comes back to me that he died.
Did you play with many loud bands in those days?
They practically were all loud. There were no microphones. I mean you had to play loud to be heard. Then we used to use a megaphone.
